question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X∼B(240,0.45),$ use the normal approximation to the binomial distribution to approximate $P(X>100).$ Round your final answer to three decimal places.

*Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.9\,$ | $\,0.1685\,$ | $\,0.1660\,$ | $\,0.1635\,$ |
| $\,-0.8\,$ | $\,0.1949\,$ | $\,0.1922\,$ | $\,0.1894\,$ |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2236\,$ | $\,0.2206\,$ | $\,0.2177\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=240$ and $p=0.45.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =240\cdot 0.45 \\  & =108 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =240\cdot (1-0.45) \\  & =132 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(240)(0.45)=108
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(240)(0.45)(1-0.45)=59.4.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(108,59.4).$

Now, we can estimate the desired probability $P(X>100).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X>100)=P(X\ge 101)≈P(Y\ge 100.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge 100.5) & =P(Z\ge \frac{100.5-108}{\sqrt{59.4}}) \\  & ≈P(Z\ge -0.97) \\  & =1-P(Z<-0.97) \\  & =1-P(Z\le -0.97) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.97) \\  & =1-0.1660 \\  & =0.834\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X>100)≈0.834.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.8347.$
